subject: MedAlign: operational evidence & onshore routing plan for opt-out
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medalign.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Brad Turner <brad.t@medalign.com>, privacy@medalign.com
Date: 2027-09-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence and routing for 'opt-out / no-train' requirement

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of our DPA review we need operational evidence that requests and responses for MedAlign customers who opt out of model improvement are: (1) excluded from any persistent model training pipelines; (2) routed to onshore storage/KMS for exportable logs; and (3) that prompt/response ownership is auditable.

Specifically we would like the following artifacts by next week:
- a high-level data flow map showing components that touch request/response data (ingress, KV/cache, ephemeral stores, batching)
- an attestation statement from Redwood on the exclusion from model improvement (no-training) and what that excludes technically (e.g., offline fine-tune, feedback loops)
- details on key residency (KMS) and export path for onshore logs (S3 endpoint, retention controls)
- a short runbook for support/ops to handle customer evidence requests (how to generate audit logs and export them)

Can you confirm feasibility and a tentative delivery date?

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of Security & Privacy, MedAlign

--
Attachment: requirements_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on intent and can provide an evidence pack. High-level plan:

- We will produce a dataflow diagram (draw.io) and a one-page operational attestation stating that opt-out traffic is excluded from model improvement pipelines.
- Onshore export: we can route audit extracts to customer-designated US S3 buckets using an onshore-forwarding lane and customer-managed KMS (or Redwood-managed onshore KMS per contract).
- Support runbook: short steps + CLI/playbook to extract and deliver logs and dataset slices.

I'll loop in Karthik (privacy/legal ops) and Laura (infra/ops) to confirm specifics and timelines. Target delivery: EOD 2027-09-27 for the full packet (dataflow + attestation + runbook). If any item requires additional legal sign-off we'll flag it earlier.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: MedAlign: operational evidence & onshore routing plan for opt-out

Thanks — quick status and proposed attestation language below.

Status: Laura confirms infra can support both customer-managed KMS in our onshore export lane and a Redwood-managed onshore KMS that uses US-only HSMs. KV cache behavior: ephemeral KV entries are not persisted to model training stores; we will document TTLs and eviction guarantees. Monica will produce the runbook skeleton and an example audit extract (json lines export).

Proposed attestation text (please review):
"Redwood Inference confirms that for MedAlign customers who have elected the 'no-training' option under their Data Processing Agreement, request and response payloads will be excluded from any persistent model-improvement pipelines or datasets used for model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation. Excluded activities include offline fine-tuning, feedback loop ingestion, and labeled dataset augmentation. Operationally, opt-out traffic will be tagged at ingress, kept isolated in ephemeral stores, and excluded from downstream model-improvement jobs. Audit extracts for opt-out traffic can be exported to customer-designated US S3 buckets with customer-managed or Redwood-provisioned US-only KMS."
Open items for legal: 1) confirm whether we need formal notarized signature for attestation or a signed letterhead PDF; 2) confirm retention wording (we must be explicit about short-term telemetry used for debugging vs. any retention for billing/abuse prevention).

I'll draft final attestation once we decide format.

—Karthik
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MedAlign: operational evidence & onshore routing plan for opt-out

Elena — attaching the evidence pack for MedAlign. See attachments and short notes below. Let me know if you want a signed PDF attestation; we can provide that on Redwood letterhead.

Attachments included:
- medalign_no-learn_evidence.pdf (one-page attestation + checklist)
- dataflow_map_v2.drawio (exported svg inside PDF)
- onshore_kms_key-policy.txt (summary of key residency options and crypto boundary)
- example_audit_export.jsonl (sample export of opt-out request/response lines; PII redacted)

Key operational notes:
- Ingress tagging: customer opt-out flag is applied at edge and carried through metadata. Tagged traffic is excluded from model-improvement ingestion jobs by a blocking filter in the ingestion pipeline.
- KV/cache: short-lived (TTL <= 2 hours) on default config for opt-out sessions and is never materialized into persistent training stores.
- Export path: audit extracts are generated by the audit service and can be exported to an S3 bucket URL provided by MedAlign. We support customer KMS (preferred) or Redwood-managed US-only KMS; both options restrict key wrapping to US HSMs.
- Support runbook: steps 1-6 to produce exports, including CLI commands, manifest filters, and verification checks.

If this satisfies your procurement checklist we can confirm delivery and include the signed attestation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Infrastructure & Compliance, Redwood Inference

--
